title: Reedy-colimit comparison for cofibrant diagrams
statement: Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with the conventions of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]: it is complete and cocomplete, weak equivalences are retract closed and satisfy two-out-of-three, and cofibrations/trivial fibrations and trivial cofibrations/fibrations form two weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. An object is cofibrant if its map from the initial object is a cofibration, as in [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations]. Let $J$ be a small Reedy category, and equip $\mathcal M^J$ with the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], whose weak equivalences are objectwise. Suppose the constant-diagram functor $\operatorname{const}_J:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M^J$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. Then the colimit functor $\operatorname{colim}_J:\mathcal M^J\to\mathcal M$, with colimits in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], sends every objectwise weak equivalence between Reedy-cofibrant diagrams to a weak equivalence and sends every Reedy-cofibrant diagram to a cofibrant object. All indexing categories and colimits are small relative to fixed universes, which may be enlarged.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12 (Ken Brown), printed pp. 6–7, and the colimit–constant adjunction argument in Lemma 5.2.6, printed pp. 126–127; generalized to any small Reedy category for which the constant functor preserves the two right classes. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this model-category result.

proof.text: Write $L=\operatorname{colim}_J$ and $R=\operatorname{const}_J$. If $\iota_j:X_j\to LX$ are the chosen colimit legs, a map $a:LX\to A$ gives the natural transformation $X\to RA$ with components $a\iota_j$. Conversely a natural transformation $X\to RA$ is a cocone and therefore determines a unique such $a$. These operations are inverse by the uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. They commute with precomposition by diagram maps and postcomposition by maps of $A$, by checking on the legs. Thus $L\dashv R$. For $J=\varnothing$ the cocone has no legs and there is exactly one map from $LX$ to every object, so $LX$ is initial.

source.place: Stacks Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit; cocones are exactly natural transformations to constants.

proof.text: Let $a:X\to Y$ be a Reedy cofibration and $q:U\to V$ a trivial fibration in $\mathcal M$. A square with left side $La$ and right side $q$ corresponds, by step 1, to a square with left side $a$ and right side $Rq$: restrict each horizontal map to its colimit legs. The hypothesis makes $Rq$ a Reedy trivial fibration, so the Reedy weak factorization system of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] gives a natural filler $Y\to RU$. Its corresponding map $LY\to U$ is a filler for the original square, because the two triangle equations hold on every colimit leg. Hence $La$ lifts against all trivial fibrations and is a cofibration by the ground weak factorization system. Repeat this same argument with $a$ a Reedy trivial cofibration and $q$ any fibration; now $Rq$ is a Reedy fibration, so $La$ lifts against all fibrations and is a trivial cofibration. This proves both preservation statements directly from the lifting-class definitions, without taking the adjunction criterion as a further lemma.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.4, printed p. 14 (adjunction and lifting); proof of Lemma 5.2.6, printed p. 127 (colimit–constant instance).

proof.text: The initial diagram $0_J$ is constant at an initial object $0$ of $\mathcal M$: each component of a transformation from it is unique. A cocone from $0_J$ to any $A$ is likewise unique, so [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] makes $L0_J$ initial, also when $J$ is empty. For a Reedy-cofibrant diagram $X$, the map $0_J\to X$ is a Reedy cofibration by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Step 2 makes $L0_J\to LX$ a cofibration. This is an initial map of $LX$, proving $LX$ cofibrant. The identification with any other chosen initial object is harmless: an isomorphism lifts against every map using its inverse, hence is a cofibration, and composing a lift for one left map with a lift for a second proves closure under composition.

source.place: Stacks Tag 002F, categories-definition-colimit, for the initial-diagram calculation; the cofibrant-object and lifting-class definitions in the cited Reedy node.

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an objectwise weak equivalence between Reedy-cofibrant diagrams. By [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] it is a weak equivalence in the Reedy model category. This category is complete and cocomplete: form any small limit or colimit at each object of $J$ and induce its structure maps by the ground universal properties; the functor laws and the universal property follow on each component. Its two weak factorization systems imply retract closure of the left and right classes: compose a lifting square with the retraction maps, lift for the larger arrow, and restrict the filler back. Thus it satisfies the model-category hypotheses of [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations]. Applying its cofibrant clause gives maps $i:X\to Z$, $p:Z\to Y$, $s:Y\to Z$ with $pi=f$, $ps=1_Y$, $p$ a trivial fibration, and $i,s$ cofibrations. Identity maps have the diagonal-lifting property against all maps (take the forced horizontal edge as filler), so are in the trivial classes and hence weak equivalences. Two-out-of-three for $pi=f$ and $ps=1_Y$ now gives that both $i$ and $s$ are weak equivalences. They are therefore Reedy trivial cofibrations.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12 (Ken Brown), printed pp. 6–7; the split factorization is supplied by the cited Brown node and the Reedy model structure by its cited node.

proof.text: Step 2 makes $Li$ and $Ls$ trivial cofibrations, hence weak equivalences. Since $(Lp)(Ls)=L(ps)=1_{LY}$, two-out-of-three in $\mathcal M$ from [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] gives that $Lp$ is a weak equivalence. Since $Lf=(Lp)(Li)$, another application of two-out-of-three gives that $Lf$ is a weak equivalence. Together with step 3 this proves both assertions; the argument imposes no fibrancy condition on the diagrams or their values.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12, printed pp. 6–7: apply the functor to the two split-factorization identities.

lean.statement: theorem reedy_colimit_comparison (M : Type u) [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [HasLimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] [(cofibrations M).HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialFibrations M)] [(trivialCofibrations M).HasFunctorialFactorization (fibrations M)] (J : Type w) [SmallCategory J] (N P : MorphismProperty J) [N.IsMultiplicative] [P.IsMultiplicative] (r : ReedyStructure N P ℕ) [diagramModel : ModelCategory (J ⥤ M)] (hReedy : diagramModel = Classical.choose (Reedy.model_structure N P r) ∧ weakEquivalences (J ⥤ M) = (weakEquivalences M).functorCategory J ∧ cofibrations (J ⥤ M) = Reedy.leftClass P (cofibrations M) ∧ fibrations (J ⥤ M) = Reedy.rightClass N (fibrations M)) (hconstF : ∀ {X Y : M} (f : X ⟶ Y), Fibration f → Fibration ((Functor.const J).map f)) (hconstTF : ∀ {X Y : M} (f : X ⟶ Y), Fibration f → WeakEquivalence f → Fibration ((Functor.const J).map f) ∧ WeakEquivalence ((Functor.const J).map f)) : (∀ {X Y : J ⥤ M} (f : X ⟶ Y), (∀ j : J, WeakEquivalence (f.app j)) → IsCofibrant X → IsCofibrant Y → WeakEquivalence (colimMap f)) ∧ (∀ X : J ⥤ M, IsCofibrant X → IsCofibrant (colimit X))
